small_guidance:
- The inner GEMM-K loop currently has only IC=64 elements per (kh,kw), so BLOCK_K=64 with a single K iteration eliminates loop overhead; restrict autotune to BLOCK_K∈{32,64} and prefer (BLOCK_M=64,BLOCK_N=128,BLOCK_K=64) or (128,64,64) with num_warps=8, num_stages=2.
- Collapse the (kh,kw,ic) reduction into a single K-dimension of length KH·KW·IC=576 so `tl.dot` sees a larger K tile and fewer index computations; precompute ih/iw inside one fused K loop instead of `static_range` over kh/kw with an inner K loop.
- Drop the final `permute(0,3,1,2).contiguous()` — return NHWC and have the model consume it, or fuse the layout transpose by writing directly to an NCHW output with strided stores; the trailing contiguous copy is a sizable fraction of the 10 ms.
large_guidance:
- Rewrite as a single fused im2col-GEMM where the K dimension is the flattened (kh·kw·ic) of length 576, allowing a 2-iteration K-loop at BLOCK_K=256 or single-shot at BLOCK_K=576-padded; this maximizes `tl.dot` arithmetic intensity versus the current 9 separate dot calls of K=64.
- Eliminate the post-kernel NHWC→NCHW contiguous copy: either keep the whole network in channels_last (set memory_format on weight and skip the permute) or have the kernel emit NCHW directly by computing output strides `(C·H·W, 1, W, 1)` and writing each (m,n) tile with appropriate strided offsets.
- Consider a persistent / split-K-free design with one program per (N, oh-tile, ow-tile, oc-tile) using BLOCK_M tiling over (oh·ow) of 15876 elements per image so the OC tile can be 128 and reused across many spatial outputs; pair with vectorized 128-bit loads on the channel-contiguous input.
